WHAT I CONCLUDED: The fix is a one-character change (side → -side) on line 1196. After applyMove(side, ...), the state's side-to-move has changed to -side. The lh_suffix block in the genmove display queried bounds2 with the mover's side, printing the bracket for the wrong colour on every move. Move choice from choose_with_check is unaffected — this is display/telemetry only.

EVIDENCE: (1) Direct inspection of the code flow: applyMove at line 1189, bounds2 at line 1196, side variable unchanged from the genmove colour. (2) T266 independently reproduced at HEAD 63e245f: 'T266's witness: after b:B3 w:C2 b:C3 it shows [16,16] where the true state is [1,16]'. (3) T277 independently confirmed: 'bounds2-after-applyMove bug prints wrong brackets'. (4) My regression test passes: builds a minimal artifact, applies b:B3, verifies bounds2 with -side returns White's bracket [-16,-1] while bounds2 with side returns Black's [1,16].

TERMINAL=TRUE FALLBACK: bounds2 returns terminal=true on its fabricated area-score fallback (lines 157, 169). No caller in gtp.zig reads .terminal from a bounds2 Row — v0, dtt0, flags0 all read other fields. The fabrication is a latent defect: if someone adds code that trusts terminal, they'll get a fabricated true on unreachable states. I did not fix it — the brief says 'either fix it or record precisely why it cannot [reach a trusting caller]' — the latter is the case: no caller trusts it.
